technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the Solo orderer as a new consensus plugin using an in-memory buffered channel and an in-RAM ledger that supports seek for history discovery.
Store chaincode friendly names as metadata managed by the lifecycle system chaincode, with a local index mapping name to chaincode ID.
Extend the existing lifecycle system chaincode to store and evaluate deployment (endorsement) policies for chaincodes.
Implement the state cache as an in-process LRU cache in the endorsement peer that fronts the state database and is invalidated on commit.
Extract the existing peer CLI into a standalone Go module that communicates with peers and orderers via gRPC, removing the dependency on RocksDB and validating peer internals.
Publish the Fabric source to GitHub by setting up an automated mirror from the Gerrit repository.
Author documentation in Markdown and publish it via a static site generator to the project site / hyperledger.org.
Use Go cross-compilation to produce platform-specific CLI binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows.
assumptions: The existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase is available, builds, and has passing tests as a baseline.
The developer is highly familiar with Go, Hyperledger Fabric internals, and distributed systems.
The Solo orderer does not require durability or crash recovery because the spec specifies an in-RAM ledger.
Friendly chaincode names are only required to be unique per channel, not globally across the network.
Deployment policies managed by the lifecycle system chaincode reuse existing signature/endorsement policy primitives.
The state cache is local to each peer and does not require distributed coherence beyond commit-time invalidation.
CLI binaries for macOS and Windows can be produced via cross-compilation without OS-specific code changes.
Documentation hosting on hyperledger.org can be achieved via existing static site tooling or GitHub Pages without new infrastructure.
